 6  # Blog Post Writing Skill
 7  
 8  ## Mode and sources
 9  
10  Read the runtime system prompt for content mode and enabled capabilities.
11  The default is **pure text**. Read at least three local notes from sources/
12  with read_source (planning.md, files.md, memory.md, approval.md). Use the
13  provided sources rather than fabricating web citations. Do not invoke
14  researcher, web_search or image tools in text mode.
15  
16  In full mode, delegate research with task(subagent_type="researcher") only
17  when search is enabled. Specify both the topic and a /research/<slug>.md
18  output path, then read the findings. Without search, use local material or
19  material supplied by the user.
20  
21  ## Output and completion
22  
23  Save text to `blogs/<slug>/post.md`. For a course report/blog, use
24  save_report(slug, content), then read_report(slug); built-in write_file and
25  read_file can be used for other content paths. Include a title, context,
26  findings, practical application and a Sources section with the local
27  filenames or enabled research URLs used. Use write_todos for the steps and
28  mark completed only after checking the saved text. Plan actual work steps;
29  do not add a task just to update the plan. Make the final write_todos update
30  in a later response than read_report, and mark all successful steps completed
31  before answering. If a tool fails, fix it before completing that step. Label
32  material drawn from the bundled course notes as synthetic and keep those
33  claims grounded in the notes. Preserve the provenance of user-provided and
34  researched material, citing the sources actually used.
35  
36  A text deliverable is complete without an image. Generate a companion image
37  only if images are enabled AND the user asks for one. Never retry an absent
38  image or search tool. Mention optional visuals only if requested.
39  
40  ## Blog Post Structure
41  
42  Every blog post should follow this structure:
43  
44  ### 1. Hook (Opening)
45  - Start with a compelling question, statistic, or statement
46  - Make the reader want to continue
47  - Keep it to 2-3 sentences
48  
49  ### 2. Context (The Problem)
50  - Explain why this topic matters
51  - Describe the problem or opportunity
52  - Connect to the reader's experience
53  
54  ### 3. Main Content (The Solution)
55  - Break into 3-5 main sections with H2 headers
56  - Each section covers one key point
57  - Include code examples, diagrams, or screenshots where helpful
58  - Use bullet points for lists
59  
60  ### 4. Practical Application
